newsitem.title: USA: Calif. receives $30 mln for damage repairs - Senator.
newsitem.headline: Calif. receives $30 mln for damage repairs - Senator.

text.p: The U.S. Department of Transportation will provide California full reimbursement for recently repaired highways damaged by this winter's floods and mudslides, U.S. Senator Barbara Boxer said on Tuesday.
California will receive $30 million in federal highway emergency relief funds to supplement the $20 million awarded earlier this month, Boxer, a California Democrat, said.
"These funds are vital in our efforts to rebuild and repair the damage to our highways and bridges," Boxer said.
The Senator said she would lobby for funding for vital flood control projects, including levee repair.
A total of 46 of California's 58 counties are now under state of emergency declarations, state officials said.
Damage estimates from the devastating New Year floods have passed $1.5 billion. Nearly 16,000 homes have been damaged or destroyed in the flooding, according to state figures.
